subject: Quant

questions.q: If ${x}$ and ${y}$ satisfy the equations $|x|+x+y=15$ and $x+|y|-y=20$, then $(x-y)$ equals
questions.explain: If $x<0$, $|x|+x=0$, so $y=15$. The second eq becomes $x+|15|-15=20$, so $x=20$, which contradicts $x<0$. Thus $x \ge 0$, and $|x|=x$. The first eq becomes $2x+y=15$. If $y<0$, $|y|=-y$, so the second eq is $x-2y=20$. Solving gives $x=10, y=-5$. Then $x-y=15$. If $y \ge 0$, the second eq is $x=20$. Then $2(20)+y=15$ gives $y=-25$, a contradiction. So $x=10, y=-5$ is the only solution. $x-y = 10 - (-5) = 15$.

questions.q: All the values of ${x}$ satisfying the inequality $\frac{1}{x+5} \le \frac{1}{2x-3}$ are
questions.explain: We solve $\frac{1}{x+5} - \frac{1}{2x-3} \le 0$. Combining fractions gives $\frac{(2x-3) - (x+5)}{(x+5)(2x-3)} \le 0$, which simplifies to $\frac{x-8}{(x+5)(2x-3)} \le 0$. The critical points are $x=-5, x=1.5, x=8$. We test the intervals: For $x>8$, all terms are positive, so fraction is positive. For $1.5 < x < 8$, the numerator is negative, denominator is positive, so fraction is negative (solution). For $-5 < x < 1.5$, numerator is negative, denominator is negative, so fraction is positive. For $x < -5$, numerator is negative, denominator is positive, so fraction is negative (solution). The solution includes the point where the numerator is zero ($x=8$) but excludes points where the denominator is zero. Thus, the solution is $(-\infty, -5) \cup (1.5, 8]$.
